mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 3 consecutive months prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 5% regimes, or IC > 0.05 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for equity valuations, driving a 60-day S&P 500 forward return up.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of UNRATE < 5% periods, or IC < -0.1 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests conflicting demand-supply dynamics that predict a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly increase > 1.5% while INDPRO monthly decrease > 2.0%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >70% of such dual-signal events, or IC > 0.08 over 1-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) above 2% for three months indicates a supply-side capacity overhang, which is expected to produce a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future demand.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >30% of GDPC1 > 2% periods, or IC < -0.05 over 6-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it signals a shift toward tighter policy, which is expected to depress equity valuations and drive a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >60% of such cross events, or IC > 0.07 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 20,000 jobs in a single month is interpreted as a labor market shock that increases uncertainty and is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in <10% of such events, or IC < -0.15 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer spending (HOUST) and retail sales (not in observable list - so omit) cannot be used; instead, a positive surprise in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend while unemployment (UNRATE) remains below 6% suggests resilient demand, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >40% of such dual-signal events, or IC < 0.05 over 1-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market that can support higher wage growth and corporate profits, thereby producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of UNRATE < 4% regimes, or IC < 0.05 over 2-year windows.
